Clay.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Clay calls follow the ground the town sits on: elk River (through the town), steep wooded hillsides rising from the bottom, Buffalo Creek joining from the north. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, opossums in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

The pattern repeats yearly: raccoon and squirrel denning in spring, bats and digging animals through summer, and a hard rodent and squirrel push into heated homes each fall. The town of Clay is a small Elk River community of older homes and modest streets on the valley floor, backed by forest. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: What is digging under Ivydale porches and outbuildings?
faqs.a: Striped skunks and opossums are the usual under-porch tenants in the river bottoms, and woodchucks take the sunnier cleared edges. We identify the den, handle the animal under the WDCA rules, and screen the opening so the space stays empty.
